data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'hillos', meaning 'hill'. In Greek mythology, the nymph Hilary was a goddess of hills and fertility. In the Christian tradition, Hilary is the name of a bishop and doctor of the Church, known for his writings on the Trinity. The name Hilliary carries the meaning “Hill, hillside, gentle one” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Hilliary usually hope their child will grow to embody hill, hillside, gentle one and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Hilary is the Anglicized version of the Latin name "Hilarius," which was used to honor Saint Hilary of Poitiers (AD 310-367), an influential bishop and doctor of the Church. Hilary was known for his theological contributions to the Christian faith, particularly regarding the nature of the Trinity. His legacy is celebrated in both the Eastern and Western Catholic Churches, and his feast day is observed on January 13th.
